i18n.en: Woe, rebellious children, says YHWH, who take counsel, but not from me, and who make a league, but not of my spirit, so as to add sin to sin;
i18n.he: ה֣וֹי בָּנִ֤ים סֽוֹרְרִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת עֵצָה֙ וְלֹ֣א מִנִּ֔י וְלִנְסֹ֥ךְ מַסֵּכָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א רוּחִ֑י לְמַ֛עַן סְפ֥וֹת חַטָּ֖את עַל־חַטָּֽאת׃

notes.official:
*Wᵉlinsōḵ massēḵāh* is the crux of the verse. The verb *nsk* I means “pour out,” and a poured libation sealed a treaty. That is the sense behind ASV “make a league” (checked), which the line keeps because the verse concerns the embassy to Egypt (vv. 2–4). A second root, *nsk* II “weave,” gives a woven covering, the sense of *massēḵāh* at 25:7 (“the veil”). NJPS follows it with “Weaving schemes,” and JPS 1917 has “form projects” (both checked). The same consonants return at v. 22 as *massēḵāh* “molten image,” from *nsk* “pour (metal).” The alternatives are recorded under overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`.

*Hôy bānîm sôrᵉrîm* “Woe, rebellious children”: before a vocative noun phrase the book prints “Woe, …” (overlay `hoy-woe-isaiah`), as at 1:4 “Woe, sinful nation” and 29:1 “Woe, Ariel.” ASV and JPS 1917 have “Woe to the rebellious children” (checked). *Wᵉlōʾ rûḥî* “but not of my spirit” keeps YHWH's *rûaḥ* in lower case (overlay `ruach-divine-spirit-lower-case-isaiah`; ASV “my Spirit”).

paragraphs.text: הַהֹלְכִים֙ לָרֶ֣דֶת מִצְרַ֔יִם וּפִ֖י לֹ֣א שָׁאָ֑לוּ לָעוֹז֙ בְּמָע֣וֹז פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלַחְס֖וֹת בְּצֵ֥ל מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: who set out to go down to Egypt, and have not asked of my mouth, to take refuge in the stronghold of Pharaoh, and to seek shelter in the shadow of Egypt!
i18n.he: הַהֹלְכִים֙ לָרֶ֣דֶת מִצְרַ֔יִם וּפִ֖י לֹ֣א שָׁאָ֑לוּ לָעוֹז֙ בְּמָע֣וֹז פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלַחְס֖וֹת בְּצֵ֥ל מִצְרָֽיִם׃

notes.official:
*Lāʿôz bᵉmāʿôz parʿōh* “to take refuge in the stronghold of Pharaoh”: the infinitive is from *ʿwz* “take refuge,” and *māʿôz* is “stronghold,” as at 17:10 and 27:5 (overlay `maoz-shalom-refuge-peace-isaiah-27`). This is the wording of JPS 1917 (checked). ASV derives both words from *ʿzz* “be strong”: “to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh” (checked). NJPS has “To seek refuge with Pharaoh.”

*Ûp̄î lōʾ šāʾālû* “and have not asked of my mouth” keeps the idiom for consulting an oracle (ASV and JPS 1917 “asked at my mouth”; NJPS “Without asking Me”; all checked). *Bᵉṣēl miṣrayim* “in the shadow of Egypt”: shade is protection, the image that v. 3 turns against them (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם מָע֥וֹז פַּרְעֹ֖ה לְבֹ֑שֶׁת וְהֶחָס֥וּת בְּצֵל־מִצְרַ֖יִם לִכְלִמָּֽה׃

i18n.en: Therefore the stronghold of Pharaoh shall become your shame, and the shelter in the shadow of Egypt your humiliation.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם מָע֥וֹז פַּרְעֹ֖ה לְבֹ֑שֶׁת וְהֶחָס֥וּת בְּצֵל־מִצְרַ֖יִם לִכְלִמָּֽה׃

notes.official: The stronghold and the shade of v. 2 return as *bōšeṯ* “shame” and *kᵉlimmāh* “humiliation” (ASV and JPS 1917 “confusion”; NJPS “chagrin”; checked). *Māʿôz* is “stronghold” (overlay `maoz-shalom-refuge-peace-isaiah-27`); that entry's clause on refuge and peace offered by YHWH does not apply here.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־הָי֥וּ בְצֹ֖עַן שָׂרָ֑יו וּמַלְאָכָ֖יו חָנֵ֥ס יַגִּֽיעוּ׃

i18n.en: For his princes are at Zoan, and his messengers reach Hanes.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־הָי֥וּ בְצֹ֖עַן שָׂרָ֑יו וּמַלְאָכָ֖יו חָנֵ֥ס יַגִּֽיעוּ׃

notes.official:
*Śārāyw … malʾāḵāyw* “his princes … his messengers”: the singular suffix has no named antecedent. It may refer to Pharaoh's officials or to the envoys of Judah's king. ASV smooths it to “their,” and JPS 1917 and NJPS keep “his” (all checked). NJPS notes an emendation that yields “kings” for *malʾāḵāyw* (checked); MT is kept.

Zoan is Tanis in the eastern Delta (NJPS note “Or ‘Tanis,’” checked), as at 19:11, 13. Hanes (*ḥānēs*) is usually identified with Heracleopolis, south of Memphis (recalled, not verified). Both names keep the ASV spelling (overlay `aram-names-isaiah`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: כֹּ֣ל הבאיש [הֹבִ֔ישׁ] עַל־עַ֖ם לֹא־יוֹעִ֣ילוּ לָ֑מוֹ לֹ֤א לְעֵ֙זֶר֙ וְלֹ֣א לְהוֹעִ֔יל כִּ֥י לְבֹ֖שֶׁת וְגַם־לְחֶרְפָּֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: All are put to shame because of a people that cannot profit them, that is no help and no profit, but a shame and also a reproach.
i18n.he: כֹּ֣ל הבאיש [הֹבִ֔ישׁ] עַל־עַ֖ם לֹא־יוֹעִ֣ילוּ לָ֑מוֹ לֹ֤א לְעֵ֙זֶר֙ וְלֹ֣א לְהוֹעִ֔יל כִּ֥י לְבֹ֖שֶׁת וְגַם־לְחֶרְפָּֽה׃ (ס)

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere. The consonantal text has הבאיש (*hiḇʾîš*, “made to stink,” that is, became odious), and the Masoretes read הֹבִישׁ (*hōḇîš*, “put to shame”). The line follows the qere (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`), as do ASV and JPS 1917 “ashamed” and NJPS “shall come to shame” (checked). The two words differ by one letter. The ketiv uses the idiom of Gen 34:30 and Exod 5:21, where “make to stink” means “make hateful.”

*Lōʾ-yôʿîlû* “cannot profit” and its echoes recur three times in vv. 5–6. They form the refrain of the oracle.

paragraphs.text: מַשָּׂ֖א בַּהֲמ֣וֹת נֶ֑גֶב בְּאֶרֶץ֩ צָרָ֨ה וְצוּקָ֜ה לָבִ֧יא וָלַ֣יִשׁ מֵהֶ֗ם אֶפְעֶה֙ וְשָׂרָ֣ף מְעוֹפֵ֔ף יִשְׂאוּ֩ עַל־כֶּ֨תֶף עֲיָרִ֜ים חֵֽילֵהֶ֗ם וְעַל־דַּבֶּ֤שֶׁת גְּמַלִּים֙ אֽוֹצְרֹתָ֔ם עַל־עַ֖ם לֹ֥א יוֹעִֽילוּ׃

i18n.en: The oracle concerning the beasts of the South. Through a land of trouble and anguish, from where come the lioness and the lion, the viper and the fiery flying serpent, they carry their riches on the shoulders of young donkeys, and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people that cannot profit them.
i18n.he: מַשָּׂ֖א בַּהֲמ֣וֹת נֶ֑גֶב בְּאֶרֶץ֩ צָרָ֨ה וְצוּקָ֜ה לָבִ֧יא וָלַ֣יִשׁ מֵהֶ֗ם אֶפְעֶה֙ וְשָׂרָ֣ף מְעוֹפֵ֔ף יִשְׂאוּ֩ עַל־כֶּ֨תֶף עֲיָרִ֜ים חֵֽילֵהֶ֗ם וְעַל־דַּבֶּ֤שֶׁת גְּמַלִּים֙ אֽוֹצְרֹתָ֔ם עַל־עַ֖ם לֹ֥א יוֹעִֽילוּ׃

notes.official:
*Maśśāʾ bahămôṯ negeḇ* “The oracle concerning the beasts of the South”: the heading follows ASV and JPS 1917 (“The burden of the beasts of the South,” checked), with “oracle” for *maśśāʾ* (overlay `massa-oracle-superscription-isaiah`) and “the South” for *negeḇ*, as at 21:1 (overlay `oracle-names-isaiah-21`). The heading is obscure. NJPS prints “The ‘Beasts of the Negeb’ Pronouncement” and notes that the meaning is uncertain and that an emendation yields “Through the wasteland of the Negeb” (checked). MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). The heading may be a catchword taken from the first line of the poem, like other headings in chs. 21–22 (recalled, not verified).

The setting is the caravan route through the southern desert to Egypt, *ʾereṣ ṣārāh wᵉṣûqāh* “a land of trouble and anguish” (central `eretz`). *Śārāp̄ mᵉʿôp̄ēp̄* is “a fiery flying serpent,” the venomous snake of 14:29 and Num 21:6, not the throne attendants of ch. 6 (overlay `seraphim-burning-ones-isaiah`). NJPS marks its “roaring king-beast” for *layiš* as uncertain (checked); ASV has “the lioness and the lion” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: וּמִצְרַ֕יִם הֶ֥בֶל וָרִ֖יק יַעְזֹ֑רוּ לָכֵן֙ קָרָ֣אתִי לָזֹ֔את רַ֥הַב הֵ֖ם שָֽׁבֶת׃

i18n.en: As for Egypt, they help in vain and to no purpose; therefore I have called her Rahab who sits still.
i18n.he: וּמִצְרַ֕יִם הֶ֥בֶל וָרִ֖יק יַעְזֹ֑רוּ לָכֵן֙ קָרָ֣אתִי לָזֹ֔את רַ֥הַב הֵ֖ם שָֽׁבֶת׃

notes.official:
*Rahaḇ hēm šāḇeṯ*: Rahab is the name of the sea monster subdued by YHWH (51:9; Ps 89:11 [Eng. 89:10]; Job 26:12), and at Ps 87:4 it is a name for Egypt. The line keeps MT and the proper name with ASV, “Rahab who sits still” (checked; overlay `rahab-sea-monster-name-isaiah`). JPS 1917 takes *rahaḇ* as a common noun, “arrogancy that sitteth still” (checked); the noun means “storm, arrogance” (BDB, recalled). NJPS renders “They are a threat that has ceased” and notes that the meaning is uncertain and that an emendation yields “Disgrace and chagrin” (checked). Other proposals redivide the words, for example *rahaḇ hammošbāt* “Rahab brought to a standstill” (not verified). MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

The line omits *hēm* “they,” as ASV does. Literally the phrase reads “Rahab, they — a sitting still.” The name of a power from the old combat poems is applied to an ally that will do nothing. That combat cluster is documented under central `chaoskampf-sea-conflict-cross-corpus-ugaritic-akkadian-hebrew-bible`, and the line names the monster without adding anything from the myth.

*Heḇel wārîq yaʿzōrû* “they help in vain and to no purpose”: *heḇel*, “breath, vapor,” is used adverbially (ASV and JPS 1917 “helpeth in vain”; NJPS “the help of Egypt shall be vain and empty”; checked). Targum Jonathan paraphrases the second half quite differently (checked; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`). “Egypt” follows overlay `aram-names-isaiah`.

paragraphs.text: עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא כָתְבָ֥הּ עַל־ל֛וּחַ אִתָּ֖ם וְעַל־סֵ֣פֶר חֻקָּ֑הּ וּתְהִי֙ לְי֣וֹם אַחֲר֔וֹן לָעַ֖ד עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: Now go, write it before them on a tablet, and inscribe it on a scroll, that it may be for the time to come, for ever and ever.
i18n.he: עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא כָתְבָ֥הּ עַל־ל֛וּחַ אִתָּ֖ם וְעַל־סֵ֣פֶר חֻקָּ֑הּ וּתְהִי֙ לְי֣וֹם אַחֲר֔וֹן לָעַ֖ד עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

notes.official:
*Wᵉʿal-sēp̄er ḥuqqāh* “and inscribe it on a scroll” is a change from the draft's “in a book.” *Sēp̄er* is any written document, and the book renders it “scroll” at 29:11–18 (overlay `sefer-sealed-scroll-isaiah-29`, extended here). ASV and JPS 1917 have “in a book,” NJPS “in a record” (all checked). The tablet (*lûaḥ*, as at 8:1) and the scroll are two surfaces for one text, which is to outlast its hearers. *ʿAl* is rendered “on.”

*Lᵉyôm ʾaḥărôn lāʿaḏ ʿaḏ-ʿôlām* “for the time to come, for ever and ever”: MT points *lāʿaḏ* “for ever,” and ASV and JPS 1917 follow it. NJPS repoints *lᵉʿēḏ* “a witness,” citing the Targum (its note, checked), and Targum Jonathan reads “for a witness before me in the day of judgment for ever” (checked on Sefaria). The line keeps MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *Yôm ʾaḥărôn* is “a later day,” the future; the line does not turn it into an end-time “last day” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י עַ֤ם מְרִי֙ ה֔וּא בָּנִ֖ים כֶּחָשִׁ֑ים בָּנִ֕ים לֹֽא־אָב֥וּ שְׁמ֖וֹעַ תּוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: For it is a rebellious people, lying children, children who would not hear the teaching of YHWH;
i18n.he: כִּ֣י עַ֤ם מְרִי֙ ה֔וּא בָּנִ֖ים כֶּחָשִׁ֑ים בָּנִ֕ים לֹֽא־אָב֥וּ שְׁמ֖וֹעַ תּוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

notes.official: *Tôraṯ YHWH* “the teaching of YHWH” (overlay `torah-teaching-isaiah`): JPS 1917 has “the teaching,” NJPS “The instruction,” and ASV “the law” (all checked). In context the *tôrāh* is the word that the seers of v. 10 are told not to give. *Bānîm kᵉḥāšîm* “lying children” follows ASV and JPS 1917; NJPS has “Faithless children.”

paragraphs.text: אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמְר֤וּ לָֽרֹאִים֙ לֹ֣א תִרְא֔וּ וְלַ֣חֹזִ֔ים לֹ֥א תֶחֱזוּ־לָ֖נוּ נְכֹח֑וֹת דַּבְּרוּ־לָ֣נוּ חֲלָק֔וֹת חֲז֖וּ מַהֲתַלּֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: who say to the seers, “Do not see,” and to the visionaries, “Do not see for us visions of what is right; speak to us smooth things, see visions of deceptions;
i18n.he: אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמְר֤וּ לָֽרֹאִים֙ לֹ֣א תִרְא֔וּ וְלַ֣חֹזִ֔ים לֹ֥א תֶחֱזוּ־לָ֖נוּ נְכֹח֑וֹת דַּבְּרוּ־לָ֣נוּ חֲלָק֔וֹת חֲז֖וּ מַהֲתַלּֽוֹת׃

notes.official:
*Lārōʾîm … wᵉlaḥōzîm*: both nouns mean “one who sees,” the first from *rʾh* “see,” the second from *ḥzh* “see (in vision).” The verse has no *nāḇîʾ* “prophet.” ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS print “to the seers … to the prophets” and render the verbs *teḥĕzû* and *ḥăzû* as “prophesy” (all checked). The line changes the draft so that both roots stay visible: “the seers … ‘Do not see,’” and “the visionaries … ‘Do not see for us visions …’” (overlay `roeh-chozeh-seer-visionary-isaiah`). At 29:10 the book prints *nᵉḇîʾîm* “the prophets” and *ḥōzîm* “the seers.” Printing “the prophets” here for *ḥōzîm* would give that English word to two Hebrew nouns in neighbouring chapters. *Rōʾeh* is the older title explained at 1 Sam 9:9.

*Nᵉḵōḥôṯ* “what is right” means straightforward things (ASV and JPS 1917 “right things”; NJPS “truth”). *Ḥălāqôṯ* “smooth things” are flatteries. *Mahăṯallôṯ* “deceptions” occurs only here, from *tll* “mock, deceive” (ASV “deceits”; JPS 1917 and NJPS “delusions”; all checked; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: ס֚וּרוּ מִנֵּי־דֶ֔רֶךְ הַטּ֖וּ מִנֵּי־אֹ֑רַח הַשְׁבִּ֥יתוּ מִפָּנֵ֖ינוּ אֶת־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: turn aside from the way, swerve from the path, make the Holy One of Israel cease from before us.”
i18n.he: ס֚וּרוּ מִנֵּי־דֶ֔רֶךְ הַטּ֖וּ מִנֵּי־אֹ֑רַח הַשְׁבִּ֥יתוּ מִפָּנֵ֖ינוּ אֶת־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

notes.official: *Minnê* is a poetic form of *min* “from.” *Hašbîṯû mippānênû ʾeṯ-qᵉḏôš yiśrāʾēl* “make the Holy One of Israel cease from before us” follows ASV and JPS 1917: the hearers want the prophet to stop speaking in that name (NJPS “Let us hear no more / About the Holy One of Israel!”; checked). The quotation that began in v. 10 closes here.

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יַ֥עַן מָֽאָסְכֶ֖ם בַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַֽתִּבְטְחוּ֙ בְּעֹ֣שֶׁק וְנָל֔וֹז וַתִּֽשָּׁעֲנ֖וּ עָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Therefore thus says the Holy One of Israel: Because you reject this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and rely on it,
i18n.he: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יַ֥עַן מָֽאָסְכֶ֖ם בַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַֽתִּבְטְחוּ֙ בְּעֹ֣שֶׁק וְנָל֔וֹז וַתִּֽשָּׁעֲנ֖וּ עָלָֽיו׃

notes.official: *Bᵉʿōšeq wᵉnālôz* “in oppression and perverseness” follows ASV and JPS 1917; NJPS has “that which is fraudulent and tortuous” (checked). An emendation of *ʿōšeq* to *ʿiqqēš* “crooked,” to pair with *nālôz* “devious,” has been proposed (not verified). MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`). The messenger formula is not set in quotation marks (overlay `title-and-meta-conventions-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֗ן יִֽהְיֶ֤ה לָכֶם֙ הֶעָוֺ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה כְּפֶ֣רֶץ נֹפֵ֔ל נִבְעֶ֖ה בְּחוֹמָ֣ה נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־פִּתְאֹ֥ם לְפֶ֖תַע יָב֥וֹא שִׁבְרָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: therefore this iniquity shall be to you like a breach ready to fall, bulging out in a high wall, whose breaking comes suddenly, in an instant.
i18n.he: לָכֵ֗ן יִֽהְיֶ֤ה לָכֶם֙ הֶעָוֺ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה כְּפֶ֣רֶץ נֹפֵ֔ל נִבְעֶ֖ה בְּחוֹמָ֣ה נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־פִּתְאֹ֥ם לְפֶ֖תַע יָב֥וֹא שִׁבְרָֽהּ׃

notes.official: *Heʿāwōn hazzeh* “this iniquity” (central `avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword`). The image is of a bulging wall: *pereṣ nōp̄ēl* “a breach ready to fall,” *niḇʿeh* “bulging out” (ASV and JPS 1917 “swelling out”), whose collapse comes *piṯʾōm lᵉp̄eṯaʿ* “suddenly, in an instant.”

paragraphs.text: וּ֠שְׁבָרָהּ כְּשֵׁ֨בֶר נֵ֧בֶל יוֹצְרִ֛ים כָּת֖וּת לֹ֣א יַחְמֹ֑ל וְלֹֽא־יִמָּצֵ֤א בִמְכִתָּתוֹ֙ חֶ֔רֶשׂ לַחְתּ֥וֹת אֵשׁ֙ מִיָּק֔וּד וְלַחְשֹׂ֥ף מַ֖יִם מִגֶּֽבֶא׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And he shall break it as a potters' jar is broken, smashed without sparing, so that among its fragments not a shard shall be found to take fire from the hearth, or to scoop water from the cistern.
i18n.he: וּ֠שְׁבָרָהּ כְּשֵׁ֨בֶר נֵ֧בֶל יוֹצְרִ֛ים כָּת֖וּת לֹ֣א יַחְמֹ֑ל וְלֹֽא־יִמָּצֵ֤א בִמְכִתָּתוֹ֙ חֶ֔רֶשׂ לַחְתּ֥וֹת אֵשׁ֙ מִיָּק֔וּד וְלַחְשֹׂ֥ף מַ֖יִם מִגֶּֽבֶא׃ (פ)

notes.official: *Kᵉšēḇer nēḇel yôṣᵉrîm* “as a potters' jar is broken”: *nēḇel* is a storage jar (ASV “potter's vessel”; NJPS “an earthen jug”; checked), and *yôṣᵉrîm* is plural, “potters” (overlay `yotser-potter-clay-image-isaiah`). The subject of *ûšᵉḇārāh* is not expressed; ASV and JPS 1917 supply “he.” *Ḥereś* is the shard that is too small *laḥtôṯ ʾēš miyyāqûḏ* “to take fire from the hearth” or *laḥśōp̄ mayim miggebeʾ* “to scoop water from the cistern” (NJPS “from a puddle”; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י כֹֽה־אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּשׁוּבָ֤ה וָנַ֙חַת֙ תִּוָּ֣שֵׁע֔וּן בְּהַשְׁקֵט֙ וּבְבִטְחָ֔ה תִּהְיֶ֖ה גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֖א אֲבִיתֶֽם׃

i18n.en: For thus says the Lord YHWH, the Holy One of Israel: In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and in trust shall be your strength. But you would not,
i18n.he: כִּ֣י כֹֽה־אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּשׁוּבָ֤ה וָנַ֙חַת֙ תִּוָּ֣שֵׁע֔וּן בְּהַשְׁקֵט֙ וּבְבִטְחָ֔ה תִּהְיֶ֖ה גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֖א אֲבִיתֶֽם׃

notes.official:
*Bᵉšûḇāh wānaḥaṯ tiwwāšēʿûn* “In returning and rest you shall be saved”: *šûḇāh* occurs only here. ASV takes it from *šûḇ* “return,” and the line follows it. JPS 1917 has “In sitting still” and NJPS “by stillness” (both checked). These relate the noun to *yšḇ* “sit” or to a separate root meaning “be still” (recalled, not verified), which would pair well with *naḥaṯ* “rest” and *hašqēṭ* “quietness.” The line does not decide whether the return is political (from the alliance with Egypt) or religious (repentance), just as the book leaves *šûḇ* open at 10:21 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

*Bᵉḇiṭḥāh* is “in trust” (ASV and JPS 1917 “confidence”). *Kî kōh ʾāmar* “For thus says”: the messenger formula is the same as in v. 12, and the line prints “thus says,” as the book does at every other *kōh ʾāmar* (7:7; 10:24; 22:15; 29:22; 42:5 and elsewhere). ASV and JPS 1917 have “thus said” here (checked; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`). *ʾĂḏōnāy YHWH* is “the Lord YHWH” (overlay `adonai-yhwh-compound-isaiah-25`), and the formula is unquoted (overlay `title-and-meta-conventions-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֨אמְר֥וּ לֹא־כִ֛י עַל־ס֥וּס נָנ֖וּס עַל־כֵּ֣ן תְּנוּס֑וּן וְעַל־קַ֣ל נִרְכָּ֔ב עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִקַּ֥לּוּ רֹדְפֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: and you said, “No, for we will flee upon horses” — therefore you shall flee; and, “We will ride upon the swift” — therefore those who pursue you shall be swift.
i18n.he: וַתֹּ֨אמְר֥וּ לֹא־כִ֛י עַל־ס֥וּס נָנ֖וּס עַל־כֵּ֣ן תְּנוּס֑וּן וְעַל־קַ֣ל נִרְכָּ֔ב עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִקַּ֥לּוּ רֹדְפֵיכֶֽם׃

notes.official: The verse is built on two echoes. *ʿAl-sûs nānûs* “we will flee upon horses” is answered by *ʿal-kēn tᵉnûsûn* “therefore you shall flee.” *ʿAl-qal nirkāḇ* “we will ride upon the swift” is answered by *ʿal-kēn yiqqallû rōḏᵉp̄êḵem* “those who pursue you shall be swift.” ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS agree on the sense (checked).

paragraphs.text: אֶ֣לֶף אֶחָ֗ד מִפְּנֵי֙ גַּעֲרַ֣ת אֶחָ֔ד מִפְּנֵ֛י גַּעֲרַ֥ת חֲמִשָּׁ֖ה תָּנֻ֑סוּ עַ֣ד אִם־נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם כַּתֹּ֙רֶן֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֔ר וְכַנֵּ֖ס עַל־הַגִּבְעָֽה׃

i18n.en: A thousand at the rebuke of one; at the rebuke of five you shall flee, until you are left like a beacon on the top of a mountain, and like a signal on a hill.
i18n.he: אֶ֣לֶף אֶחָ֗ד מִפְּנֵי֙ גַּעֲרַ֣ת אֶחָ֔ד מִפְּנֵ֛י גַּעֲרַ֥ת חֲמִשָּׁ֖ה תָּנֻ֑סוּ עַ֣ד אִם־נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם כַּתֹּ֙רֶן֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֔ר וְכַנֵּ֖ס עַל־הַגִּבְעָֽה׃

notes.official:
*ʾElep̄ ʾeḥāḏ mippᵉnê gaʿăraṯ ʾeḥāḏ* “A thousand at the rebuke of one”: the first line has no verb. ASV supplies “[shall flee],” JPS 1917 prints “shall flee,” and NJPS keeps the ellipsis, “One thousand before the shout of one” (all checked). The line keeps it too. *Gᵉʿārāh* is “rebuke” (JPS 1917; ASV “threat”; NJPS “shout”). The verse reverses the promise that one would chase a thousand (Deut 32:30; Lev 26:8).

*Kattōren* “like a beacon”: *tōren* is a pole or mast (33:23 “mast”; Ezek 27:5). ASV and JPS 1917 have “beacon” and NJPS “mast” (checked); the line keeps “beacon” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`). *Kannēs* “like a signal” (overlay `nes-signal-isaiah`; ASV and JPS 1917 “ensign”).

paragraphs.text: וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם וְלָכֵ֥ן יָר֖וּם לְרַֽחֶמְכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אֱלֹהֵ֤י מִשְׁפָּט֙ יְהוָ֔ה אַשְׁרֵ֖י כָּל־ח֥וֹכֵי לֽוֹ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And therefore YHWH waits to be gracious to you, and therefore he will be exalted to have compassion on you. For YHWH is a God of justice; blessed are all who wait for him.
i18n.he: וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם וְלָכֵ֥ן יָר֖וּם לְרַֽחֶמְכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אֱלֹהֵ֤י מִשְׁפָּט֙ יְהוָ֔ה אַשְׁרֵ֖י כָּל־ח֥וֹכֵי לֽוֹ׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*Yārûm lᵉraḥemḵem* “he will be exalted to have compassion on you” follows ASV and JPS 1917. NJPS has “He will arise to pardon you,” taking *rûm* as rising to act (checked). The verse turns on *ḥkh* “wait”: YHWH *yᵉḥakkeh* “waits,” and those who wait (*ḥôḵê*) for him are blessed. *ʾĔlōhê mišpāṭ* is “a God of justice” (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`).

*ʾAšrê kol-ḥôḵê lô* “blessed are all who wait for him”: ASV has “blessed,” JPS 1917 and NJPS “Happy” (checked). The book prints “Blessed” for *ʾašrê* at 32:20, and the line matches it (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: כִּי־עַ֛ם בְּצִיּ֥וֹן יֵשֵׁ֖ב בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בָּכ֣וֹ לֹֽא־תִבְכֶּ֗ה חָנ֤וֹן יָחְנְךָ֙ לְק֣וֹל זַעֲקֶ֔ךָ כְּשָׁמְעָת֖וֹ עָנָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: For a people shall dwell in Zion, at Jerusalem; you shall weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the sound of your outcry; when he hears it, he will answer you.
i18n.he: כִּי־עַ֛ם בְּצִיּ֥וֹן יֵשֵׁ֖ב בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בָּכ֣וֹ לֹֽא־תִבְכֶּ֗ה חָנ֤וֹן יָחְנְךָ֙ לְק֣וֹל זַעֲקֶ֔ךָ כְּשָׁמְעָת֖וֹ עָנָֽךְ׃

notes.official:
*Kî-ʿam bᵉṣiyyôn yēšēḇ bîrûšālāim* “For a people shall dwell in Zion, at Jerusalem”: MT points *yēšēḇ* as a finite verb, and ASV follows it (“For the people shall dwell,” checked). JPS 1917 (“O people that dwellest in Zion at Jerusalem”) and NJPS (“O people in Zion, dwellers of Jerusalem”) read a vocative, as with the participle *yōšēḇ* (checked). MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

*Lᵉqôl zaʿăqeḵā* “at the sound of your outcry” (central `zaaqah-outcry-of-the-oppressed`; ASV “at the voice of thy cry”). From here on the people are addressed as a singular “you.”

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַ֨ן לָכֶ֧ם אֲדֹנָ֛י לֶ֥חֶם צָ֖ר וּמַ֣יִם לָ֑חַץ וְלֹֽא־יִכָּנֵ֥ף עוֹד֙ מוֹרֶ֔יךָ וְהָי֥וּ עֵינֶ֖יךָ רֹא֥וֹת אֶת־מוֹרֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And though the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teacher shall no longer be hidden, but your eyes shall see your teacher;
i18n.he: וְנָתַ֨ן לָכֶ֧ם אֲדֹנָ֛י לֶ֥חֶם צָ֖ר וּמַ֣יִם לָ֑חַץ וְלֹֽא־יִכָּנֵ֥ף עוֹד֙ מוֹרֶ֔יךָ וְהָי֥וּ עֵינֶ֖יךָ רֹא֥וֹת אֶת־מוֹרֶֽיךָ׃

notes.official:
*Môreyḵā* (twice) is the crux, and the line changes the draft's “your teachers” to the singular “your teacher.” ASV reads a plural, “thy teachers” (checked). The verb *yikkānēp̄*, however, is singular. The form itself can be singular, because nouns ending in *-eh* sometimes keep a *yod* before the suffix (GKC §93ss; recalled, not verified). This chapter has a case three verses later: *miqneyḵā* “your livestock” takes the singular verb *yirʿeh* (v. 23). JPS 1917 “thy Teacher” and NJPS “your Guide” read the singular (checked). So does Rashi, who explains “your Teacher” as “the Holy One, blessed be He” (checked on Sefaria). Targum Jonathan paraphrases the clause as YHWH's Shekhinah, no longer withdrawn from the sanctuary (checked).

The line prints the singular in lower case. The grammar is followed, and the referent stays open: God, or a human teacher such as the prophet. The book also prints divine epithets in lower case (“the rock of Israel,” v. 29). *Yikkānēp̄* occurs only here and is linked with *kānāp̄* “wing, edge”: hidden in a corner, or behind the edge of a garment, as Rashi has it (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

*Leḥem ṣar ûmayim lāḥaṣ* “the bread of adversity and the water of affliction” is ASV's construct reading (checked). JPS 1917 (“sparing bread and scant water”) and NJPS (“meager bread and scant water”) take the nouns as describing a short ration, as at 1 Kgs 22:27 (checked). *ʾĂḏōnāy* is “the Lord” (overlay `adonai-standalone-title-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: וְאָזְנֶ֙יךָ֙ תִּשְׁמַ֣עְנָה דָבָ֔ר מֵֽאַחֲרֶ֖יךָ לֵאמֹ֑ר זֶ֤ה הַדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ לְכ֣וּ ב֔וֹ כִּ֥י תַאֲמִ֖ינוּ וְכִ֥י תַשְׂמְאִֽילוּ׃

i18n.en: and your ears shall hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way, walk in it,” when you turn to the right and when you turn to the left.
i18n.he: וְאָזְנֶ֙יךָ֙ תִּשְׁמַ֣עְנָה דָבָ֔ר מֵֽאַחֲרֶ֖יךָ לֵאמֹ֑ר זֶ֤ה הַדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ לְכ֣וּ ב֔וֹ כִּ֥י תַאֲמִ֖ינוּ וְכִ֥י תַשְׂמְאִֽילוּ׃

notes.official: The voice of the teacher of v. 20 now speaks from behind the hearer and keeps them on the road. *Kî ṯaʾămînû wᵉḵî ṯaśmᵉʾîlû* are verbs formed from “right hand” and “left hand.” *Zeh hadderek lᵉḵû ḇô* “This is the way, walk in it” follows ASV and JPS 1917.

paragraphs.text: וְטִמֵּאתֶ֗ם אֶת־צִפּוּי֙ פְּסִילֵ֣י כַסְפֶּ֔ךָ וְאֶת־אֲפֻדַּ֖ת מַסֵּכַ֣ת זְהָבֶ֑ךָ תִּזְרֵם֙ כְּמ֣וֹ דָוָ֔ה צֵ֖א תֹּ֥אמַר לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And you shall defile the overlay of your carved images of silver, and the plating of your molten image of gold; you shall cast them away as an unclean thing; “Get out!” you shall say to it.
i18n.he: וְטִמֵּאתֶ֗ם אֶת־צִפּוּי֙ פְּסִילֵ֣י כַסְפֶּ֔ךָ וְאֶת־אֲפֻדַּ֖ת מַסֵּכַ֣ת זְהָבֶ֑ךָ תִּזְרֵם֙ כְּמ֣וֹ דָוָ֔ה צֵ֖א תֹּ֥אמַר לֽוֹ׃

notes.official:
*Ṣippuy pᵉsîlê ḵaspeḵā* “the overlay of your carved images of silver” (central `pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus`, “carved image”). *ʾĂp̄uddaṯ massēḵaṯ zᵉhāḇeḵā* “the plating of your molten image of gold” keeps the Hebrew singular (ASV “molten images”). *Massēḵāh* here is the cast image, from *nsk* “pour (metal)”; compare v. 1.

*Tizrēm kᵉmô dāwāh* “you shall cast them away as an unclean thing”: *zrh* is “scatter, winnow” (as in v. 24), and *dāwāh* is “sick, unwell,” used of the menstruant (Lev 15:33; 20:18). ASV has “as an unclean thing,” JPS 1917 “as one unclean,” and NJPS “like a menstruous woman” (all checked). NJPS notes that a change of vocalization yields “keep” for *tizrēm* (checked). MT is kept (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַן֩ מְטַ֨ר זַרְעֲךָ֜ אֲשֶׁר־תִּזְרַ֣ע אֶת־הָאֲדָמָ֗ה וְלֶ֙חֶם֙ תְּבוּאַ֣ת הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה דָשֵׁ֖ן וְשָׁמֵ֑ן יִרְעֶ֥ה מִקְנֶ֛יךָ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כַּ֥ר נִרְחָֽב׃

i18n.en: And he will give the rain for your seed with which you sow the ground, and bread, the produce of the ground, and it shall be rich and plentiful. In that day your livestock shall graze in broad pastures;
i18n.he: וְנָתַן֩ מְטַ֨ר זַרְעֲךָ֜ אֲשֶׁר־תִּזְרַ֣ע אֶת־הָאֲדָמָ֗ה וְלֶ֙חֶם֙ תְּבוּאַ֣ת הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה דָשֵׁ֖ן וְשָׁמֵ֑ן יִרְעֶ֥ה מִקְנֶ֛יךָ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כַּ֥ר נִרְחָֽב׃

notes.official: *ʾĂḏāmāh* is “the ground” in both clauses (central `adam-adamah`). *Wᵉhāyāh ḏāšēn wᵉšāmēn* “and it shall be rich and plentiful” (ASV “fat and plenteous”). *Miqneyḵā* “your livestock” has the *yod* form with a singular verb, the evidence used at v. 20.

paragraphs.text: וְהָאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהָעֲיָרִ֗ים עֹֽבְדֵי֙ הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה בְּלִ֥יל חָמִ֖יץ יֹאכֵ֑לוּ אֲשֶׁר־זֹרֶ֥ה בָרַ֖חַת וּבַמִּזְרֶֽה׃

i18n.en: and the oxen and the young donkeys that work the ground shall eat seasoned fodder, which has been winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.
i18n.he: וְהָאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהָעֲיָרִ֗ים עֹֽבְדֵי֙ הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה בְּלִ֥יל חָמִ֖יץ יֹאכֵ֑לוּ אֲשֶׁר־זֹרֶ֥ה בָרַ֖חַת וּבַמִּזְרֶֽה׃

notes.official: *Hāʾălāp̄îm wᵉhāʿăyārîm ʿōḇᵉḏê hāʾăḏāmāh* “the oxen and the young donkeys that work the ground” (central `adam-adamah`). *Bᵉlîl ḥāmîṣ* “seasoned fodder”: *ḥāmîṣ* occurs only here. ASV has “savory provender,” JPS 1917 “savoury provender,” and NJPS “salted fodder” (checked). Even the animals eat grain winnowed *bāraḥaṯ ûḇammizreh* “with the shovel and with the fork” (ASV; JPS 1917 and NJPS “fan”; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ עַל־כָּל־הַ֣ר גָּבֹ֗הַ וְעַל֙ כָּל־גִּבְעָ֣ה נִשָּׂאָ֔ה פְּלָגִ֖ים יִבְלֵי־מָ֑יִם בְּיוֹם֙ הֶ֣רֶג רָ֔ב בִּנְפֹ֖ל מִגְדָּלִֽים׃

i18n.en: And there shall be on every lofty mountain and on every high hill brooks, streams of water, in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ עַל־כָּל־הַ֣ר גָּבֹ֗הַ וְעַל֙ כָּל־גִּבְעָ֣ה נִשָּׂאָ֔ה פְּלָגִ֖ים יִבְלֵי־מָ֑יִם בְּיוֹם֙ הֶ֣רֶג רָ֔ב בִּנְפֹ֖ל מִגְדָּלִֽים׃

notes.official: *Pᵉlāḡîm yiḇlê-māyim* “brooks, streams of water” run on the heights. *Bᵉyôm hereḡ rāḇ binp̄ōl miḡdālîm* “in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall” follows ASV and JPS 1917. The plenty comes on the day the towers fall, the same day as in v. 26.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה אֽוֹר־הַלְּבָנָה֙ כְּא֣וֹר הַֽחַמָּ֔ה וְא֤וֹר הַֽחַמָּה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שִׁבְעָתַ֔יִם כְּא֖וֹר שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים בְּי֗וֹם חֲבֹ֤שׁ יְהוָה֙ אֶת־שֶׁ֣בֶר עַמּ֔וֹ וּמַ֥חַץ מַכָּת֖וֹ יִרְפָּֽא׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, like the light of the seven days, in the day that YHWH binds up the fracture of his people and heals the wound of its blow.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֤ה אֽוֹר־הַלְּבָנָה֙ כְּא֣וֹר הַֽחַמָּ֔ה וְא֤וֹר הַֽחַמָּה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שִׁבְעָתַ֔יִם כְּא֖וֹר שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים בְּי֗וֹם חֲבֹ֤שׁ יְהוָה֙ אֶת־שֶׁ֣בֶר עַמּ֔וֹ וּמַ֥חַץ מַכָּת֖וֹ יִרְפָּֽא׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*Kᵉʾôr šiḇʿaṯ hayyāmîm* has the article: “like the light of the seven days” (JPS 1917 and NJPS, checked). ASV drops it, “as the light of seven days” (checked). The line renders the article and no more (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`). The phrase is often taken as an explanatory gloss on *šiḇʿāṯayim* “sevenfold”: the light of seven days gathered into one. Whether the LXX lacks it was not verified. The classical readings checked on Sefaria do not agree on what the seven days are. Ibn Ezra reads “as the light of seven days joined together” (checked). Radak reads it figuratively, as if the light of the seven days of the week were one (checked); the Reviewer also found his alternative, the seven days of Solomon's dedication. b. Pesachim 68a and b. Sanhedrin 91b read the verse of the brightness of the days of the Messiah (checked by the Reviewer). Targum Jonathan and Rashi multiply: “three hundred and forty-three times,” “seven sevens” (both checked). None of these sources takes “the seven days” as the week of creation.

*ʾÔr-hallᵉḇānāh kᵉʾôr haḥammāh* “the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun” uses the poetic names *lᵉḇānāh* “the white one” and *ḥammāh* “the hot one.” The same pair is shamed before YHWH's glory at 24:23 (overlay `kavod-labanah-chammah-isaiah-24`). *Bᵉyôm ḥăḇōš YHWH ʾeṯ-šeḇer ʿammô ûmaḥaṣ makkāṯô yirpāʾ* “in the day that YHWH binds up the fracture of his people and heals the wound of its blow”: the suffix is singular and refers to the people (ASV “their wound”). The healing answers the unbound wounds of 1:5–6.

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֤ה שֵׁם־יְהוָה֙ בָּ֣א מִמֶּרְחָ֔ק בֹּעֵ֣ר אַפּ֔וֹ וְכֹ֖בֶד מַשָּׂאָ֑ה שְׂפָתָיו֙ מָ֣לְאוּ זַ֔עַם וּלְשׁוֹנ֖וֹ כְּאֵ֥שׁ אֹכָֽלֶת׃

i18n.en: Behold, the name of YHWH comes from afar, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke; his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is like a devouring fire;
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֤ה שֵׁם־יְהוָה֙ בָּ֣א מִמֶּרְחָ֔ק בֹּעֵ֣ר אַפּ֔וֹ וְכֹ֖בֶד מַשָּׂאָ֑ה שְׂפָתָיו֙ מָ֣לְאוּ זַ֔עַם וּלְשׁוֹנ֖וֹ כְּאֵ֥שׁ אֹכָֽלֶת׃

notes.official:
*Hinnēh šēm-YHWH bāʾ mimmerḥāq* “Behold, the name of YHWH comes from afar”: the name stands for YHWH himself. NJPS prints “the LORD Himself,” with the note “Lit. ‘The name of the Lord’” (checked); the line keeps the literal phrase. *Bōʿēr ʾappô* is “burning with his anger” (literally, “his nose burning”).

*Wᵉḵōḇeḏ maśśāʾāh* “and in thick rising smoke”: *maśśāʾāh* occurs only here, from *nśʾ* “lift.” ASV (“thick rising smoke”) and JPS 1917 (“thick uplifting of smoke”) take it as the rising column of smoke, as *maśʾaṯ* is the smoke signal of Judg 20:38, 40. NJPS reads “With a heavy burden” and notes that the meaning is uncertain (all checked; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`). Verses 27–33 describe a storm theophany: fire, smoke, flood, cloudburst and hail.

paragraphs.text: וְרוּח֞וֹ כְּנַ֤חַל שׁוֹטֵף֙ עַד־צַוָּ֣אר יֶֽחֱצֶ֔ה לַהֲנָפָ֥ה גוֹיִ֖ם בְּנָ֣פַת שָׁ֑וְא וְרֶ֣סֶן מַתְעֶ֔ה עַ֖ל לְחָיֵ֥י עַמִּֽים׃

i18n.en: and his breath is like an overflowing stream that reaches up to the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction; and a bridle that leads astray shall be on the jaws of the peoples.
i18n.he: וְרוּח֞וֹ כְּנַ֤חַל שׁוֹטֵף֙ עַד־צַוָּ֣אר יֶֽחֱצֶ֔ה לַהֲנָפָ֥ה גוֹיִ֖ם בְּנָ֣פַת שָׁ֑וְא וְרֶ֣סֶן מַתְעֶ֔ה עַ֖ל לְחָיֵ֥י עַמִּֽים׃

notes.official:
*Wᵉrûḥô kᵉnaḥal šôṭēp̄* “and his breath is like an overflowing stream”: “breath” under the clause of overlay `ruach-divine-spirit-lower-case-isaiah` used at 40:7. *ʿAḏ-ṣawwāʾr yeḥĕṣeh* “that reaches up to the neck” recalls the Assyrian flood of 8:8.

*Lahănāp̄āh gôyim bᵉnāp̄aṯ šāwᵉʾ* “to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction”: *nāp̄āh* is a sieve, from *nwp* “shake,” and *šāwᵉʾ* is “emptiness, worthlessness.” ASV and JPS 1917 have “the sieve of destruction” (checked), a sieve that keeps nothing back. NJPS reads “a misguiding yoke,” comparing an Arabic word, and notes that the meaning of the line is uncertain (checked; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`). *Resen maṯʿeh* “a bridle that leads astray” (ASV “a bridle that causeth to err”) is put on the jaws of the peoples.

paragraphs.text: הַשִּׁיר֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם כְּלֵ֖יל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ־חָ֑ג וְשִׂמְחַ֣ת לֵבָ֗ב כַּֽהוֹלֵךְ֙ בֶּֽחָלִ֔יל לָב֥וֹא בְהַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־צ֥וּר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: You shall have a song as in the night when a feast is hallowed, and gladness of heart, as when one goes with the flute to come to the mountain of YHWH, to the rock of Israel.
i18n.he: הַשִּׁיר֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם כְּלֵ֖יל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ־חָ֑ג וְשִׂמְחַ֣ת לֵבָ֗ב כַּֽהוֹלֵךְ֙ בֶּֽחָלִ֔יל לָב֥וֹא בְהַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־צ֥וּר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

notes.official: *ʾEl-ṣûr yiśrāʾēl* “to the rock of Israel”: the divine epithet *ṣûr* is printed in lower case (overlay `yah-tzur-olamim-everlasting-rock-isaiah-26`, whose rationale already names this verse). ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS print “the Rock of Israel” (checked). *Kᵉlêl hiṯqaddeš-ḥāḡ* “as in the night when a feast is hallowed”: a festival begun at night. *Bᵉḥālîl* is “with the flute,” as at 5:12. NJPS moves “with timbrels, and with lyres” here from v. 32 (its note, checked); the line keeps the Hebrew order.

paragraphs.text: וְהִשְׁמִ֨יעַ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ה֣וֹד קוֹל֗וֹ וְנַ֤חַת זְרוֹעוֹ֙ יַרְאֶ֔ה בְּזַ֣עַף אַ֔ף וְלַ֖הַב אֵ֣שׁ אוֹכֵלָ֑ה נֶ֥פֶץ וָזֶ֖רֶם וְאֶ֥בֶן בָּרָֽד׃

i18n.en: And YHWH will cause the grandeur of his voice to be heard, and will show the descent of his arm, in furious anger and the flame of a devouring fire, with cloudburst and tempest and hailstones.
i18n.he: וְהִשְׁמִ֨יעַ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ה֣וֹד קוֹל֗וֹ וְנַ֤חַת זְרוֹעוֹ֙ יַרְאֶ֔ה בְּזַ֣עַף אַ֔ף וְלַ֖הַב אֵ֣שׁ אוֹכֵלָ֑ה נֶ֥פֶץ וָזֶ֖רֶם וְאֶ֥בֶן בָּרָֽד׃

notes.official:
*Hôḏ qôlô* “the grandeur of his voice” is a change from the draft and from ASV and JPS 1917 “his glorious voice”; NJPS has “His majestic voice” (all checked). *Hôḏ* means “splendour, majesty, vigour” (BDB; HALOT; recalled) and occurs in Isaiah only here (not concordance-verified). Every usual English word for it is already reserved in this book for another noun: “glory” for *kāḇôḏ*, “splendor” for *hāḏār*, “majesty” for *gāʾôn* and *gēʾûṯ* of God, “honor” for *tip̄ʾereṯ*, and “beauty” for *ṣᵉḇî*. “Grandeur” gives *hôḏ* its own word, and the noun is kept rather than made into an adjective (overlay `hod-grandeur-isaiah`). The choice awaits the founder's decision; the alternative is NJPS's “majesty,” with the overlap recorded.

*Naḥaṯ zᵉrôʿô* “the descent of his arm” (ASV and JPS 1917 “the lighting down of his arm”; NJPS “the sweep of His arm”; checked). *Nep̄eṣ wāzerem wᵉʾeḇen bārāḏ* “with cloudburst and tempest and hailstones”: *nep̄eṣ*, from *npṣ* “shatter,” is the bursting storm. JPS 1917 has “a bursting of clouds,” ASV “a blast,” and NJPS “tempest” for *nep̄eṣ*, “rainstorm” for *zerem* (all checked; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־מִקּ֥וֹל יְהוָ֖ה יֵחַ֣ת אַשּׁ֑וּר בַּשֵּׁ֖בֶט יַכֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: For at the voice of YHWH Assyria shall be dismayed; with the rod he will strike.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־מִקּ֥וֹל יְהוָ֖ה יֵחַ֣ת אַשּׁ֑וּר בַּשֵּׁ֖בֶט יַכֶּֽה׃

notes.official:
*Kî-miqqôl YHWH yēḥaṯ ʾaššûr* “For at the voice of YHWH Assyria shall be dismayed”: *ḥtt* means “be shattered” or “be dismayed.” ASV and JPS 1917 have “dismayed,” NJPS “cowed” (checked).

*Baššēḇeṭ yakkeh* “with the rod he will strike”: the subject is not named. ASV makes it YHWH: “with his rod will he smite [him].” JPS 1917 calls Assyria “The rod with which He smote,” and NJPS has “Assyria, who beats with the rod” (all checked), recalling the rod of 10:5, 24. The line keeps the Hebrew's unmarked “he” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`). “Assyria” follows overlay `aram-names-isaiah`.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כֹּ֤ל מַֽעֲבַר֙ מַטֵּ֣ה מֽוּסָדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ עָלָ֔יו בְּתֻפִּ֖ים וּבְכִנֹּר֑וֹת וּבְמִלְחֲמ֥וֹת תְּנוּפָ֖ה נִלְחַם־בה [בָּֽם׃]

i18n.en: And every passing of the appointed staff, which YHWH lays upon him, shall be with timbrels and lyres; and in battles of brandishing he will fight against them.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֗ה כֹּ֤ל מַֽעֲבַר֙ מַטֵּ֣ה מֽוּסָדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ עָלָ֔יו בְּתֻפִּ֖ים וּבְכִנֹּר֑וֹת וּבְמִלְחֲמ֥וֹת תְּנוּפָ֖ה נִלְחַם־בה [בָּֽם׃]

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere. In *nilḥam-bāh* / *bām* the consonantal text has בה “against her/it,” and the Masoretes read בָּם “against them.” The line follows the qere (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`), with ASV and JPS 1917 “with them” (checked). NJPS has “with him” and marks the verse as uncertain (checked).

*Maṭṭēh mûsāḏāh* “the appointed staff” (ASV, JPS 1917) is literally a “staff of foundation,” the staff YHWH has destined. An emendation to *mûsārô* “of his chastisement” has been proposed (not verified). *Kōl maʿăḇar* “every passing” (ASV “every stroke”; JPS 1917 “every place where … shall pass”). *Bᵉṯuppîm ûḇᵉḵinnōrôṯ* “with timbrels and lyres” are the instruments of 5:12 and 24:8 (ASV “tabrets and harps”): each blow falls to the music of the festival of v. 29. In *bᵉmilḥămôṯ tᵉnûp̄āh* “in battles of brandishing,” *tᵉnûp̄āh* is the waving, the word used for the wave offering (Exod 29:24), here the brandished arm or weapon (ASV “battles with the brandishing [of his arm]”; JPS 1917 “battles of wielding”; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־עָר֤וּךְ מֵֽאֶתְמוּל֙ תָּפְתֶּ֔ה גַּם־הוא [הִ֛יא] לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הוּכָ֖ן הֶעְמִ֣יק הִרְחִ֑ב מְדֻרָתָ֗הּ אֵ֤שׁ וְעֵצִים֙ הַרְבֵּ֔ה נִשְׁמַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ כְּנַ֣חַל גָּפְרִ֔ית בֹּעֲרָ֖ה בָּֽהּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For a Topheth has been prepared from of old; it too is made ready for the king; he has made it deep and wide; its pyre is fire and wood in abundance; the breath of YHWH, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־עָר֤וּךְ מֵֽאֶתְמוּל֙ תָּפְתֶּ֔ה גַּם־הוא [הִ֛יא] לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הוּכָ֖ן הֶעְמִ֣יק הִרְחִ֑ב מְדֻרָתָ֗הּ אֵ֤שׁ וְעֵצִים֙ הַרְבֵּ֔ה נִשְׁמַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ כְּנַ֣חַל גָּפְרִ֔ית בֹּעֲרָ֖ה בָּֽהּ׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*Kî-ʿārûḵ mēʾeṯmûl tāp̄teh* “For a Topheth has been prepared from of old”: *tāp̄teh* occurs only here and is a form of *tōp̄eṯ*, the burning place in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned (2 Kgs 23:10; Jer 7:31–32; 19:6). ASV prints “a Topheth” and NJPS “The Topheth,” with a note on the site; JPS 1917 renders a common noun, “a hearth” (all checked). Targum Jonathan renders “Gehinnom” (checked), the later name of the valley. The chain from Hinnom to Gehenna is documented under central `gehenna-valley-of-hinnom-1-enoch-27-nt-cross-corpus`; the line keeps the place name.

Ketiv/Qere. In *gam-hûʾ* / *hîʾ* the consonantal text has the masculine הוא, and the Masoretes read the feminine הִיא, which agrees with *tāp̄teh*. The line follows the qere, “it too” (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

*Lammeleḵ hûḵān* “is made ready for the king”: MT points *meleḵ* “king,” and ASV and JPS 1917 have “for the king” (checked). NJPS reads “He too is destined for Melech” and refers to Molech (Lev 18:21; 20:2–5; checked). The consonants allow the allusion, because Topheth was the site of the *mōleḵ* rite (2 Kgs 23:10; Jer 32:35 names the Hinnom valley and Molech), and the king of Assyria is the victim on either reading. Targum Jonathan reads “the eternal King hath prepared it” (checked). The line keeps MT's pointing (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-30`).

*Heʿmîq hirḥiḇ mᵉḏurāṯāh ʾēš wᵉʿēṣîm harbēh* “he has made it deep and wide; its pyre is fire and wood in abundance” follows ASV's division. NJPS takes *mᵉḏurāṯāh* as the subject of a passive, “His firepit has been made both wide and deep” (checked). *Nišmaṯ YHWH kᵉnaḥal gāp̄rîṯ* “the breath of YHWH, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it” (central `gophrit-va-esh-destruction-formula`, “sulfur”; ASV “brimstone”).
